title: Redwood security review - SSO/SCIM & RBAC (Enterprise)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (ClearHealth - Head of IT Security), Sara Li (ClearHealth - Product Security), Jamal Singh (ClearHealth - DevOps)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we scheduled 60 mins to run through SSO, SCIM provisioning patterns and how our RBAC maps to your groups, plus a bit on audit logs and KMS. quick intros?
[00:12] Michael: mike here -- head of IT security at clearhealth. i'll drive the security requirements, and i'll bring jamal in for devops specifics.
[00:18] Sara: sarah, product security, mainly here to understand access models and how least privilege will look for our product teams.
[00:25] Jamal: jamal, devops, i'll look at provisioning, network, and KMS integration.
[00:30] Priya: priya from redwood, i'll cover the SCIM/provisioning and RBAC details, and deep dive on audit/export options.
[00:36] Alex: great. mike, quickly - what's your IdP? okta? azure ad?
[00:40] Michael: yeah we're on okta, using SCIM and group sync today for most SaaS. we want everything to be centrally managed; deprovisioning must be immediate.
[00:48] Alex: okta is our most common pathway. we support SAML 2.0 SP-initiated and IdP-initiated, SCIM 2.0 for provisioning, group push and group membership sync. i'll run through required attributes.
[01:05] Priya: on SCIM we basically recommend two flows: 1) SCIM-based provisioning (recommended) so we can do automatic create/update/deactivate, and 2) JIT (just-in-time) provisioning for lighter setups but it doesn't handle deprovisioning well. for enterprise we push SCIM.
[01:25] Jamal: can you map Okta groups to roles in redwood? we need devs to have deploy rights but not billing or key management.
[01:33] Priya: absolutely. we have role templates: Admin, Developer, Operator, ReadOnly, and you can create custom roles. mapping is group-to-role via SCIM group membership or SAML attribute (groups claim). ex: okta group "clearhealth-redwood-developers" -> Developer role which includes create/deploy but excludes billing:manage and kms:manage.
[01:55] Michael: what about least-privilege for service accounts? we have CI/CD bots that need tokenized access for deploys.
[02:03] Priya: for service accounts we recommend short-lived tokens + scoped API keys. Redwood supports API keys with fine-grained scopes and you can rotate or scope via role bindings. for extra security you can put those keys in your secret manager and use our audit logs to track key usage.
[02:20] Sara: auditing — how long do you retain logs? we need 1 year for some workflows and the ability to export to our SIEM.
[02:27] Alex: default cloud-hosted retention is 90 days, but enterprise plans support longer retention or log export. we can stream audit events to your S3 bucket, or to syslog/SIEM via a secure webhook/forwarder. for compliance customers we often set up archive to S3 with lifecycle rules you manage.
[02:48] Michael: and are audit entries immutable? tamper-proof? we need cryptographic integrity or at least write-once export.
[02:55] Priya: logs in our system are append-only and access-controlled; for cryptographic immutability we recommend exporting to your own S3 with server-side encryption + object lock for WORM-like retention if required.
[03:10] Jamal: KMS - can we bring our own CMK? or do you manage keys?
[03:15] Alex: we support customer-managed keys (CMK) for certain enterprise packages. envelope encryption is used: data encrypted with DEKs and those DEKs encrypted with your KMS CMK. we have integrations with AWS KMS and external HSMs for private deployments.
[03:32] Michael: certificate rotation and key rotation processes? can priya describe?
[03:36] Priya: yes - keys are rotated at the KMS level; you control rotation policies. for SAML certs (the SSO signing cert) we have a metadata endpoint and support rolling certs. we recommend you rotate on a schedule and upload new metadata; we also support automatic metadata fetch for some IdPs but many customers prefer manual to control timing.
[03:57] Sara: session timeouts - can we enforce session length from the IdP?
[04:00] Alex: session enforcement is layered: the IdP enforces SSO session and we also have token TTLs. best practice is to enforce MFA and session expiry at IdP and keep API tokens short-lived.
[04:15] Michael: scoping roles - can you show an example policy language?
[04:20] Priya: sure - we have a role editor in the console. for example Developer = [models:invoke, routes:deploy, logs:view], Operator = [routes:manage, infra:scale], BillingAdmin = [billing:read, billing:manage], KMSAdmin = [keys:manage]. you can combine or remove permissions.
[04:45] Jamal: is there a way to prevent redeploys from prod unless a group approval occurs?
[04:50] Priya: not currently an approval workflow in the base RBAC but you can gate CI to require an approver via your pipeline. we are working on policy-conditional actions (we noted customer ask).
[05:05] Alex: ok, switching to SAML specifics. for SP config you'll need our ACS URL and Entity ID; we'll send metadata. we support attributes: email, firstName, lastName, groups. group claim mapping is important for role mapping.
[05:20] Michael: do you support group push from Okta (pushed groups) vs groups claim? which is more reliable?
[05:26] Priya: pushed groups via SCIM are more reliable for provisioning and deprovisioning. groups claim is lighter weight and fine if you only need assertions during login, but it doesn't create users or handle lifecycle. for least-privilege we recommend SCIM + group-to-role mapping.
[05:45] Alex: i'll note that and send our SCIM provisioning guide.
[05:48] Sara: metadata—self-signed certs ok, or do you need a trusted CA?
[05:52] Priya: SAML uses signing certs for assertions; self-signed is typical and fine as long as you provide metadata. for mTLS between systems we use CA-signed certs in private deployments.
[06:05] Michael: what's the typical time to onboard with SCIM + RBAC mapping? we have 200+ employees and multiple teams.
[06:12] Alex: typically 1-2 weeks to test and validate with Okta in a staging tenant; for full production rollout including audit and CMK setup expect 3-6 weeks depending on contract and network setup.
[06:25] Jamal: network-wise - are there static IPs we need to allowlist for your hosted product?
[06:30] Priya: yes for hosted we provide a set of egress IPs; for private deployments you run inside your VPC. we'll share the IP CIDR ranges; if you need dedicated ingress we can set up private link or VPN options.
[06:45] Michael: data residency — can we pin data to us-west-2?
[06:49] Alex: yes, enterprise customers can pick region for data at rest. hosted tenants can be regionally isolated; private deployments give you on-prem control. we'll note your preference.
[07:00] Sara: regulatory - do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001?
[07:03] Alex: yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001. we'll send the summary reports and an NDA/controls matrix if needed.
[07:12] Michael: would we get SOC2 evidence collection help?
[07:16] Priya: we can provide our controls matrix, typical evidence artifacts, and a security POC package. for in-depth audits we coordinate with our security team.
[07:28] Jamal: about deprovisioning — how immediate is it when Okta deactivates a user?
[07:33] Priya: SCIM deactivation is near real-time; usually within seconds to a minute. JIT deactivation relies on SSO session expiry and token TTLs so it's not immediate.
[07:44] Alex: let's demo the mapping — priya, can you walk through console quickly?
[07:48] Priya: sure - (screen share note: priya narrates the console) console -> org settings -> auth -> SSO: upload metadata or fill entity id, ACS URL. below is SCIM token and provisioning toggle. group mapping page shows list of roles and upstream groups. e.g., map okta group "clearhealth-devs" -> Developer. you can also set default role for new users.
[08:20] (audio blip)
[08:22] Sara: sorry lost you for a sec, but seeing the group mapping. can default role be none so we don't give privileges until we explicitly map?
[08:29] Priya: yes, default can be none; we set 'no access' and only grant via explicit group mapping for least-privilege.
[08:35] Michael: where do we manage service account scopes?
[08:38] Priya: APIs -> service accounts -> create key -> assign role(s) and set TTL. keys show last used and you can revoke.
[08:45] Jamal: if someone has billing:view but we need to restrict to billing:read only for a specific group, can that be a custom role?
[08:51] Priya: yes, create custom role with billing:read and assign to group. roles are additive; if a user is in multiple groups the union of permissions apply so be careful about overlapping groups.
[09:05] Michael: audit exports — does exported data include token usage and API calls with IP? we need IP, actor, timestamp, resource.
[09:13] Priya: exported events include actor (user/service account), action, resource id, timestamp, source IP, and request payload summary. for PII we redact request bodies unless you enable more verbose logs for debug.
[09:28] Alex: a question from our side — do you need SAML NameID as email or persistent id?
[09:33] Michael: we prefer email as it's our canonical.
[09:36] Priya: that's supported; we map email to username and it's the canonical id in the tenant.
[09:40] Jamal: provisioning rate limits — okta might push many users during initial sync. can SCIM handle bulk?
[09:46] Priya: our SCIM endpoint supports bulk (paged) operations with retries. for large onboards we often ask customers to stage in batches to avoid rate limits, and we can temporarily raise limits for the onboarding window.
[10:00] Sara: we have compliance requirement to show last access time per user. is that in your audit?
[10:06] Priya: yes, last active timestamp is tracked and available in exports; console shows last login and last API usage per user.
[10:14] Michael: any known gaps? external IDP group attributes sometimes truncate long names; okta-specific?
[10:20] Priya: occasionally group names with unicode or very long names can be normalized. we recommend short canonical group names for mapping. we also handle group id mapping rather than name to be resilient.
[10:36] Alex: time check — about 40 minutes left; do we want to schedule the SCIM test now?
[10:41] Jamal: yes, let's schedule. want priya to create a staging tenant. we'll provide an Okta test org and test accounts.
[10:49] Alex: action item for priya to provision demo tenant and enable SCIM.
[10:54] Priya: noted. i'll provision and send invite. i'll also include a test plan: create user, add to group, confirm role, remove user, confirm deprovision.
[11:05] Michael: for CMK and KMS, we need a deeper session. can we do a technical deep dive on key rotation and envelope flow?
[11:12] Alex: yes, we'll schedule a KMS deep dive with our infra security engineer. target next week.
[11:18] Sara: any blockers around data residency for us-west-2?
[11:22] Alex: none, we support region pinning; for hosted we'll ensure tenant is provisioned in us-west-2. private on-prem gives full control but is heavier lift.
[11:30] Jamal: last Q - audit log access controls; who in your org can see raw logs?
[11:35] Priya: only SRE/security roles have access. we provide role-based admin controls and can scope visibility. for enterprise we can limit logs to a security mailbox or push to your S3.
[11:46] Michael: ok that covers it. can you also send an architecture sketch for the onboarding flow?
[11:50] Alex: yes i'll include a sequence diagram in the follow-up.
[11:55] Sara: thanks, this was helpful.
[11:58] Alex: great - recap of next steps in chat, we'll follow up with docs and tenant. thanks everyone.

Meeting end.
